issues.legal_issue: A High Court exercising constitutional writ jurisdiction may correct jurisdictional errors and errors apparent on the face of the record, but does not act as an appellate court to reappraise facts.
material_facts: The High Court found that the rehabilitation authorities had cancelled an auction sale without complying with the required notice procedure.
The Supreme Court examined the official record and concluded that the finding of non-compliance was not erroneous.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was entitled to correct the apparent legal error and did not impermissibly substitute its factual judgment for that of the authorities.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 226 of the Constitution, the High Court does not sit as a court of appeal to substitute its judgment for that of the empowered authorities, but may correct jurisdictional errors and errors apparent on the face of the record. Under S.L. Hegde & Ors. v. M.B. Tirumale, an error is apparent if it can be brought to the surface without prolonged argument.

predicates.high_court_writ_review: The matter is a proceeding in which a High Court reviews an administrative decision through constitutional writ jurisdiction.
predicates.jurisdictional_error: The authority acted outside the jurisdiction conferred on it.
predicates.apparent_error_without_prolonged_argumen: The record discloses an error that can be identified without prolonged argument.
predicates.high_court_may_correct_the_error_without: The High Court may correct the jurisdictional or apparent error without acting as an appellate court on the facts.

issues.definition: When a High Court reviews an administrative decision through writ jurisdiction, it may correct a jurisdictional error or an error apparent without prolonged argument, while leaving factual reappraisal to the authority.

issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court does not interfere merely because another view of the facts is possible when reviewing a High Court’s discretionary decision under constitutional writ jurisdiction.
material_facts: The appeal challenged the High Court’s decision to grant writ relief against administrative orders cancelling an earlier auction sale.
The Supreme Court found no injustice to the appellant and no reason to disturb the High Court’s decision.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court declined to interfere with the High Court’s exercise of discretion.
issues.legal_principle: It is a settled rule of practice under Article 136 of the Constitution that the Supreme Court does not interfere with the High Court’s discretionary exercise of powers under Article 226 merely because two factual views are possible. Interference requires a matter of public or general importance, or an error of law causing such gross injustice to an individual that it touches the Court’s conscience.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal_from_discretionary_writ_order and two_views_possible_on_facts and not (public_or_general_importance or gross_injustice_from_error_of_law)

predicates.special_leave_appeal_from_discretionary_: The proceeding is a special-leave appeal challenging a High Court’s discretionary decision in writ jurisdiction.
predicates.two_views_possible_on_facts: The facts permit more than one possible view.
predicates.public_or_general_importance: The question in the appeal involves a matter of public or general importance.
predicates.gross_injustice_from_error_of_law: An error of law has caused such gross injustice to an individual that it touches the Court’s conscience.
predicates.supreme_court_does_not_interfere: The Supreme Court declines to disturb the High Court’s discretionary decision.

issues.definition: The Supreme Court does not interfere in a special-leave appeal from a discretionary writ decision merely because the facts permit two views when neither public or general importance nor gross injustice from an error of law is present.

issues.legal_issue: An auction sale cannot be cancelled and the purchaser’s deposit forfeited for non-payment of the balance purchase price without service of the notice required by the governing auction rules.
material_facts: The purchaser’s bid was accepted and the acceptance letter stated that any balance purchase money would be communicated after scrutiny of compensation claims.
The authorities cancelled the sale and forfeited the deposit on the ground that the balance price had not been paid.
The purchaser had complied with the notice requirement identified by the High Court, but the notice required by the relevant further sub-rule was not issued or served.
The High Court found that the required notice condition had not been met, and the Supreme Court held that this conclusion was not erroneous.
issues.conclusion: The authorities lacked jurisdiction to cancel the sale and forfeit the deposit without the required notice.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 90 of the Displaced Persons Compensation and Rehabilitation Rules, 1955 makes service of the notice specified in the applicable sub-rules a condition precedent to cancellation of a sale and forfeiture of the initial deposit. The Court upheld the High Court’s conclusion that the required notice had not been issued or served.

rule.if: auction_sale_cancellation_proceeding and purchaser_met_initial_notice_requirement and required_notice_not_served and sale_cancelled_for_balance_nonpayment

predicates.auction_sale_cancellation_proceeding: The proceeding concerns an authority’s cancellation of an auction sale.
predicates.purchaser_met_initial_notice_requirement: The purchaser complied with the applicable initial notice requirement.
predicates.required_notice_not_served: The authority did not issue or serve the further notice required before cancellation.
predicates.sale_cancelled_for_balance_nonpayment: The authority cancelled the sale for alleged non-payment of the balance purchase price.
predicates.cancellation_and_forfeiture_lack_jurisdi: The authority has no jurisdiction to cancel the sale or forfeit the purchaser’s deposit.

issues.definition: When an auction sale is cancelled for non-payment after the purchaser has met the initial notice requirement but the further required notice was not served, the cancellation and forfeiture lack jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: An appeal concerning the cancellation of an auction sale cannot be disposed of without the prescribed hearing procedure, and a request for additional time to pay must be considered judicially rather than treated as merely administrative.
material_facts: The purchaser appealed the cancellation and sought additional time to pay the balance purchase price.
The appellate authority dismissed the appeal as an administrative matter without fixing a hearing date and informing the purchaser of it.
The High Court held that this procedure contravened the rule applying the relevant civil-procedure appeal provisions, and the Supreme Court recounted that conclusion while upholding the writ relief.
issues.conclusion: The appellate authority’s disposal of the appeal without the prescribed hearing procedure and judicial consideration of the request for more time was invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 105 of the Displaced Persons Compensation and Rehabilitation Rules, 1955 applies, so far as applicable, the procedure in Order XLI of the Code of Civil Procedure to appeals and revisions. The Court referred to Hiralal Kher v. The Chief Settlement Commissioner, New Delhi, on the hearing requirement, and stated that a request for extension of time required judicial and judicious consideration rather than treatment as an administrative matter.

predicates.administrative_appeal_proceeding: The proceeding is an appeal from an administrative decision concerning an auction sale.
predicates.appeal_decided_without_notice_of_hearing: The appellate authority decided the appeal without fixing a hearing date and informing the appellant of it.
predicates.extension_request_treated_as_merely_admi: The appellant sought additional time, but the authority treated that request as merely administrative rather than deciding it judicially.
predicates.appeal_disposal_is_invalid: The appellate authority’s disposal of the appeal is invalid.

issues.definition: When an administrative appeal is decided without notice of a hearing and a request for additional time is treated as merely administrative, the appeal’s disposal is invalid.
